Definitions needed to interpret the dataset analysis
2/3/4-bit across all observed group sizes, evaluated separately within each model/checkpoint context.
3/4-bit removes the strongest floor effects; full grid includes 1, 1.58, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8-bit.
Accuracy ratio = HQQ top-1 / matched baseline top-1. Ratios above 1 are retained.
Absolute drop = baseline top-1 minus HQQ top-1 in percentage points.
Rank 1 is the highest retention ratio. Ties receive average rank.
Agreement between dataset rankings while model and checkpoint kind remain fixed and quantization settings change.
Agreement between model/checkpoint rankings at the same bit and group size.
Both ordering directions occur for a dataset pair across settings in the same context.
All 4,320 matched cells are retained. This is the primary analysis.
Eleven contexts were removed after observing low or anomalous baselines. It cannot replace the primary analysis.
Each cell has one seed. Quantization settings are repeated measurements, not independent training replications.
Results describe HQQ and dataset-specific checkpoints. They do not establish an intrinsic dataset property or generalize to all PTQ methods.
